title: Harvesting the Variance Risk Premium in Nuclear and Energy Equities: A Short-Put Portfolio Derisking Strategy

extraction.methodology_summary: The strategy constructs a systematic short-put portfolio across a universe of nuclear and energy-adjacent equities by writing cash-secured put options. Realized volatility is estimated using a GARCH(1,1) model with consensus parameters and compared against ATM implied volatility to measure the variance risk premium. Positions target 0.30-delta and 45-day DTE, and are rebalanced or exited based on specific take-profit, stop-loss, or expiration rules.
extraction.universe: 39 nuclear and energy-adjacent equities with option coverage from a total universe of 45 tickers
key_findings: A statistically significant positive variance risk premium exists in the majority of nuclear and energy equities with option coverage.

An unconditional short-put strategy achieves an annualized return of 18.7% with a Sharpe ratio of 7.81 and a maximum drawdown near zero, significantly outperforming the equal-weight stock benchmark on a risk-adjusted basis.
The unconditional put strategy achieved positive calendar-year returns in all 25 years of the sample.
A GARCH-filtered conditional variant (IV/RV threshold >= 1.10) maintains a high Sharpe ratio of 2.63 with a 7.7% maximum drawdown, albeit with fewer trades.
limitations: The backtest uses option mid-prices throughout without modeling realistic bid-ask execution costs.
Cash-secured capital earns no T-bill return, understating opportunity cost post-2022.
The universe is fixed at today's list of survivors, introducing survivorship and look-ahead bias.
Exit prices assume fills at the first daily mid satisfying the stop or take-profit condition, which may understate gap risk on adverse overnight moves.
